When provenance is incomplete, decisions cannot be traced, tests or releases cannot be reproduced, or artifacts are fragmented
When implementation needs author assistance, normative and informative material conflict, key audiences cannot use the standard, or examples are inadequate
When critical responsibilities are unfilled, editorial or testing capacity is insufficient, decision authority is unclear, or development depends on one person
When Development has materially altered the development case itself
When stakeholders have not seen the candidate, review windows were insufficient, changes were not communicated, or feedback remains ungathered
When evidence is too weak, interoperability is unproven, important scenarios are unexercised, or regression confidence is insufficient
When the candidate works but maintenance is too expensive, adoption burden is excessive, stewardship is fragile, or tooling is unsustainable
When Development reveals missing actors, unseen infrastructure, a new control dependency, or materially different stakeholder impacts

When new actors, infrastructure, or control relationships emerge
When harm, incompatibility, governance failure, or major ecosystem change warrants immediate review
When a serious defect requires corrective work before waiting for formal Review
When adoption friction is primarily explanatory rather than structural
